title: Claude Agent SDK: Subagents and Session Store

questions.question: What is the difference between the Anthropic Client SDK and the Claude Agent SDK?
options: Client SDK is a paid Enterprise tier of the Messages API; Agent SDK is the free open-source package instead
Client SDK runs only on Python; Agent SDK adds first-class support for every other language Anthropic ships today
Client SDK is raw Messages API; Agent SDK is the Claude Code harness shape with built-in tools, MCP, hooks, subagents, and session store
There is no real difference; both SDKs wrap the exact same underlying agent loop and shared tool registry surface
questions.explanation: Client SDK gives you the loop; Agent SDK ships the loop pre-built.

questions.question: What are the two documented purposes of subagents?
options: Caching and rate limiting across every tool call the subagent makes across a run
Logging and metrics collection for the orchestrator's full audit trail
Authentication and authorization checks before a subagent can spawn
Parallelization (concurrent work) and context isolation (own context window)
questions.explanation: Subagents run independent work concurrently and preserve the orchestrator's context budget by isolating context.

questions.question: Which method is NOT part of the session store surface?
options: compile_prompt, which builds the system prompt from templates and variables
append, which adds a brand new message turn to the current active session log
load, which restores the full conversation history for a given session
list_subkeys, which lists every subagent key nested under a session
questions.explanation: Session store ships append, load, list_sessions, delete, list_subkeys; compile_prompt is not a session API.

questions.question: Which is NOT a Claude Agent SDK lifecycle hook?
options: PreToolUse, which gates or audits a tool call before it runs
PreEmbedding, which runs before the SDK computes any vector embedding
PreCompact, which runs right before the session undergoes context compaction
SessionStart, which runs setup logic when a new session begins
questions.explanation: Hooks include PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart/End, UserPromptSubmit, PreCompact, Stop, Notification. PreEmbedding is not a hook.

questions.question: How does trace context propagate across the agent and CLI subprocess?
options: Through shared files on disk that both processes poll continuously
Only via the provider's dashboard, with no local trace propagation
Through W3C trace context headers passed into the CLI subprocess
Only through environment variables set once at process startup
questions.explanation: OTel spans on the caller propagate into the CLI subprocess via W3C trace context, so the whole multi-process run is one trace.

questions.question: What is subagent over-spawn and when does it happen?
options: Forgetting to call SessionEnd after every single subagent finishes its work
Spawning a subagent before the SessionStart hook has fully finished running
Spawning more subagents at once than the machine has CPU cores available
Spawning 100 subagents for 100 tiny tasks where overhead dominates; batch instead
questions.explanation: Subagents have overhead; batch small tasks instead of spawning one each.

questions.question: What does Claude Managed Agents trade off against the self-hosted SDK?
options: Control for managed infrastructure (long-running async, built-in prompt caching, built-in compaction)
Latency for cost, since Managed Agents always run on cheaper spot instances by default and nothing else
Tools for memory, since Managed Agents drop all custom tool registration entirely
Tracing for streaming, since Managed Agents cannot stream any partial output at all
questions.explanation: Managed Agents is the hosted alternative for long-running async work; less control, less ops surface.
